study.question: With observed pooled and ordinal historical actions retained, does match-aligned action content improve validation click AUC beyond a fixed duplicate of advertisement-content summaries, and does that conditional increment depend on task-specific versus shared residual readout?
study.hypothesis: Observation: r0032 task both/erased match-action endpoints scored 0.6662444304756373/0.6637536617254408; r0033 shared both/erased endpoints scored 0.6647487996065942/0.6618160448245677. Both raw and scaled channels help relative to erasure, but the task-minus-shared action-availability interaction is -0.0004419860318299884, not evidence for a larger task-specific action effect. The incumbent remains g0-r0022-support_rotated_attached at 0.666753547526167; the shared DIN reference is 0.6555440824200336. Those whole-model gains cannot be apportioned causally by subtracting unmatched branches. Mechanism hypothesis: target-match/action association adds useful information conditional on existing item, pool and ordinal inputs. If this content, rather than merely active coordinates or duplicated-content conditioning, matters, observed match-action rows should outperform fixed redundant item coordinates at matched learned width. The dependence on operational task readout is a separate two-sided interaction question. No performance improvement over the incumbent is required.

study.proposed_difference: Add architecture selector match_action_content in {observed,item_duplicate}. In item_duplicate mode, before the existing availability gate replace only action coordinates of summary rows 0 and 4 by the FP32 sum of the same row's F item-field embedding vectors divided by sqrt(F), cast back to summary dtype. This is a deterministic linear function of item coordinates already in the residual input, with no new lookup/parameters/RNG, no action-derived scale and no new raw information. Observed mode returns the incoming action tensor unchanged, so its executed tensor graph is inherited. Ordinal action rows and all item coordinates remain unchanged; original availability gates apply after replacement. Cross both content modes with task/shared residual readout. Four standalone modules, no training-loss or host changes.
predictions: Primary two-sided measured contrasts are G_task=AUC(match_observed_task)-AUC(match_itemdup_task) and G_shared=AUC(match_observed_shared)-AUC(match_itemdup_shared). Positive repeated gaps surviving controls would support conditional action-content utility; effect magnitudes are not assumed.

Readout interaction is I=G_task-G_shared. Prior erasure interaction is negative at one seed. There is no predeclared claim that task routing amplifies action utility, and a readout main effect is insufficient for interaction.

The item replacement may recover some erased-endpoint loss via conditioning even though it adds no information; full recovery would weaken the interpretation that the erased-coordinate loss specifically measures feedback content.

At common state, only raw/scaled match action coordinates may change with content, while pool/scorer inputs, ordinal actions, item summaries, counts, masks and auxiliary ownership stay fixed. Zero match support yields zero replacements from the already masked item rows.

Expected parameters are 32129765 in all cells with unchanged learned shape. Replacement adds a small fixed summary reduction, not a new sequence/scorer pass. Measure actual training wall/allocated GPU time, memory, examples and inference throughput/latencies; no efficiency claim follows from FLOP intuition.

Report all four AUC/Logloss values, separate auxiliary mean and frozen history-length slices with sample/positive/negative counts. Other hour/frequency/composition/unseen slices are only exploratory if authorized host metadata exists; do not infer unavailable counts or create new inputs.
falsifiers: Either fresh content replacement matches/exceeds observed AUC within uncertainty: weakens feedback-specific interpretation for that routing and replacement. A nonrepeatable gap remains preliminary.
Interaction near zero or inconsistent across authorized repetitions/user-cluster intervals: no supported dependence of the conditional content gain on task-specific readout.

Any current-action, invalid-history or original-mask violation, changed learned construction, unauthorized auxiliary gradient, or observed bridge discrepancy invalidates attribution until repaired; it is an execution/integrity failure, not scientific counterevidence.
A future prespecified scale/optimization control closes the gap: favors conditioning/optimization explanation over information content. This first replacement does not exhaust those controls.
